newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia drafts plan for U.S.-Estonian power j/v.
newsitem.headline: Estonia drafts plan for U.S.-Estonian power j/v.

text.p: The Estonian government said on Friday it had drafted a cooperation and development agreement between state-run electricity company Eesti Energia (Estonia Energy) and U.S. NRG Generating International.
The draft agreement calls for Eesti Energia to form a joint venture with NRG.
The two sides signed a Memorandum Of Understanding in March in which NRG pledged to invest up to $250 million in Estonia Energy.
"We are discussing the prospects for three power plants, which the joint venture will run," Estonian Minister of Economics Andres Lipstock told Reuters.
He said there was a lot of work to be done before any final agreement was reached.
"The negotiations will be tough," he said. "The government will not guarantee NRG any markets and the price of electricity will be set by Estonian law."
Estonia Energy is the main supplier of electricity in the smallest of the three Baltic states and its outdated plants require considerable investment.
The company's turnover in 1995 was 2.28 billion kroons and its assets total 1.9 billion kroons.
